title: Delhi HC Upholds Rs 197 Crore Electricity Tax on NTPC's Auxiliary Consumption at Badarpur Plant
case_name: NTPC Ltd. v. South Delhi Municipal Corporation
card_summary: A Division Bench dismissed NTPC's challenge to a Rs 197.15 crore electricity tax demand on its Badarpur plant for June 2006 to October 2018. Section 113(2)(d) of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 taxes consumption, not generation, so power NTPC drew from its own station to run the plant counts as consumption. The court upheld the 1962 tax bye-laws and rejected the delay objection.
card_tip: A generating station drawing power to run its own plant cannot treat that auxiliary draw as outside the municipal electricity tax net; consumption, not generation, triggers the levy.
verification_notes: Citation 2026:DHC:9358-DB, writ number W.P.(C) 4144/2022, judgment reserved 6 October 2026 and reported pronounced 28 October 2026, the Rs 197,15,84,639 figure, the June 2006-October 2018 period, the Section 113(2)(d) consumption-vs-generation holding, the Bye-law 3(3) challenge and the delay challenge are each confirmed across Verdictum, LiveLaw Biz and SupremeToday. None of the three reports names the individual judges on the Division Bench, so the bench composition is not stated here.
